title: English revival bands and King Colyer
summary: Jiles thinks Ken Colyer played closest to old Dixieland and that Chris Barber's band skipped around when playing a rag.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: What about these Englishmen that you've heard play the young guys, what do you think of them as compared with the old times?

You mean those Englishmen coming down here, is that practically the one you're talking about? I had a band from England that King Collier played with, would you be referring to them? Yeah, what about him?
Well I was thinking about King Collier and different guys like that.

Well I think King Collier to me, not because I made the record with him, but I think he played more near to the old Dixieland and these guys that he was playing with. What I can recall, to one of the numbers that this Englishman played, one of the rags that they tried to play and I couldn't catch because when they called me when they was playing over the air they played some of their numbers to let the people know what they had. And one of the numbers that we played, and they started off and when they got to the middle they jumped, and they got to something else and they jumped and they went out in the ending to make you know what they was playing, and that wasn't so hot.
Which band was this? Is this Chris Ballmer or which one do you remember?
